summary: Code review FAIL. One Blocking issue found: BookmarksPanelView.axaml line 27 uses ObjectConverters.IsNull on Bookmarks.Count (an int), which can never be null. The IsNull converter always returns false for a non-nullable int, making the 'No bookmarks for this movie.' empty-state TextBlock permanently invisible.

All other dimensions are clean: BookmarkItemViewModel, BookmarksPanelViewModel, FakeBookmarkSettingsService, FakeBookmarkRepository, and test coverage are all well-implemented and consistent with project patterns.
Remaining observations are low-priority: CommandParameter=0 AXAML placeholder, AddBookmark insert delegation pattern noted.

comments.note: BLOCKING: BookmarksPanelView.axaml line 27 — `IsVisible="{Binding Bookmarks.Count, Converter={x:Static ObjectConverters.IsNull}}"`. Bookmarks.Count is a non-nullable int, which when boxed to object is never null. ObjectConverters.IsNull always returns false for any int value (including 0), so the empty-state TextBlock ('No bookmarks for this movie.') is permanently invisible regardless of the collection size. Compare with correct usages in MoviesListView.axaml (CoverImageBitmap: Bitmap?) and TagEditorView.axaml (DeleteImpact: nullable ref type) where IsNull applies to nullable reference types. SUGGESTED FIX: (A) Add `public bool HasNoBookmarks => Bookmarks.Count == 0;` to BookmarksPanelViewModel, subscribe to `Bookmarks.CollectionChanged += (_, _) => OnPropertyChanged(nameof(HasNoBookmarks));` in the production constructor, and change the AXAML to `IsVisible="{Binding HasNoBookmarks}"`. (B) Alternatively, use a `BoolConverters.Not` approach with a helper that converts int != 0 to bool — but Option A is the most idiomatic for this codebase.

BookmarksPanelView.axaml: Rating TextBlock uses `IsVisible="{Binding Rating, Converter={x:Static ObjectConverters.IsNotNull}}"`. Since Rating is a non-nullable int, this is the same misuse — IsNotNull always returns true for int (it's never null), so the rating TextBlock is always visible even when Rating == 0 (unrated). Consider a similar ViewModel property `public bool HasRating => Rating > 0;` or binding to `Rating` with a value converter that treats 0 as false.

BookmarksPanelView.axaml: Add Bookmark button has CommandParameter hardcoded to '0' as a design-time placeholder. This is clearly documented in the AXAML comment. No blocking concern for this WP but the Navigation integration WP should replace this with a bound CurrentPlayerPositionMs property or programmatic parameter injection.

BookmarksPanelViewModel.cs: the CancellationTokenSource _cts used by LoadCommand is a plain CancellationTokenSource created at field initialization. It uses CreateLinkedTokenSource when combining with the command's own CancellationToken. This pattern is consistent with how BookmarksPanelViewModel existed before. Clean and correct.

BookmarkItemViewModel.cs: PositionLabel correctly formats PositionMs as 'hh:mm:ss' (e.g. '00:01:30'). This is the time-formatted display that is appropriately used in the panel view. Consistent with the MediaPlayer standard. Clean implementation.

comments.note: BookmarksPanelViewModel.EditBookmark: unlike LoadCommand and AddBookmarkCommand, the [RelayCommand] method has no CancellationToken parameter and does not pass _cts.Token (or a linked token) to _settingsService.ShowAsync. If the ViewModel is disposed while the edit dialog is open, the ShowAsync continuation will still run and call item.Update(updated) on an item that has been removed and disposed. In practice this is safe (Update() only sets Description/Rating, both of which remain valid), but the inconsistency with the other commands is a code smell. Consider adding `CancellationToken ct` to the method signature and passing a linked token — this would also make the pattern consistent across all commands.

RegisterCollectionNotifications() correctly documents that any future third constructor must call it. Consider also adding an assertion guard (e.g., a Debug.Assert or a private bool field toggled in the helper) to surface the omission early if a third constructor is ever added without the call. Low priority — the XML doc comment is sufficient for now.
